name: Mix session track naming conventions
description: Conventional track names used in mixing sessions, grouped by instrument family, for filename/track-name matching. Instruments and modifiers are kept in separate tables so a name like 'Snare Top 2' resolves to instrument=snare_top plus modifiers.

fields.category.id: Stable identifier for the family; categories are listed in conventional session order.
fields.category.model_label: Closest label of a common 10-class instrument-family set (sfx, woodwinds, brass, bass, strings, synth, drums, vocal, guitar, keys) for fallback agreement checks.
fields.instrument.id: Stable identifier, unique across the file.
fields.instrument.canonical: Preferred display name used when renaming.
fields.instrument.parent: Optional id of a broader instrument (kick_in -> kick) so results can be rolled up.
fields.instrument.generic: true for family-level words (Drums, Guitar, Keys); a specific match in the same category wins over a generic one.
fields.instrument.aliases: Full words or phrases. Match as whole tokens / token sequences, case-insensitive.
fields.instrument.abbreviations: Short codes. Match ONLY as a complete token, never as a substring.
fields.instrument.zh: Traditional Chinese aliases (matched as substrings after normalisation; longest first).
fields.instrument.ja: Japanese aliases (matched as substrings; longest first).

normalize: Unicode NFKC (full-width letters/digits/brackets -> half-width), keep CJK characters
Split camelCase and letter-digit boundaries: 'SnareTop2' -> 'snare top 2', 'Gtr1' -> 'gtr 1'
Drop tempo/key/date noise before matching: '\d{2,3}\s?bpm', '\b[a-g](#|b)?\s?(maj|min|m)\b', 8-digit dates
match_order: Longest phrase first (so 'bass drum' -> kick before 'bass', 'kick in' before 'kick', '古箏' before '箏')
aliases: whole-token phrases; abbreviations: exact single token only
zh / ja: substring match on the normalised string, longest first
A token consumed by an instrument match cannot be reused by another match
resolution: non-generic > generic within the same category
If two different categories remain, return both and mark the result ambiguous (do not guess; fall back to audio classification)
Words not found in any table are kept verbatim when renaming (never silently dropped)
matching_rules.numbering: Trailing numbers (1, 01, #1, (2)) are kept as the instance number: 'Tom 2', 'BV 03'.

ambiguous_terms.resolution: English sessions: song section unless combined with vox/vocal. Japanese sessions (コーラス / Cho): backing vocals.
Treat as backing vocals when it is the only instrument-like token or appears in parentheses after a song title, e.g. 'song(cho)_Track1'.
Always kick (longest phrase wins over 'bass').
With another instrument ('Piano Room') it is a mic-position modifier; alone it is drum room; with verb/rev it is a reverb return.
Orchestral context or 'french' -> French horn; pop/funk sessions -> horn section.
'blues harp' / 'harp' next to guitar-band tracks -> harmonica; otherwise harp.
Synth pad unless combined with drum/perc/sample.
'kick sub' -> kick_sub; 'sub mix'/'submix' -> bus; alone -> sub bass.
Alone or with bass/sub -> 808 bass; '808 kit' or with kick/snare/hat -> drum machine.
Instrument unless preceded by a note name.
Abbreviation only; prefer Bridge when another instrument is already present.
Kick when it is the only instrument token.
Bass by default; bari sax only next to other sax tracks.
Contrabass in orchestral sessions, cowbell otherwise.
Keys by default.
Trombone unless the session has a talkback track.
Vocal by default.
Modifier only; 'Lead' alone is not an instrument (could be vocal, guitar or synth).
Instrument when followed by a number or drum context.
Use the longer phrase; 'bells' alone -> glockenspiel.
A full-mix print only when no instrument is present; treat 'mix' followed by a number as a version label.
Sound effects in Japanese sessions.
Japanese generic word for drum; taiko only with 和太鼓 or festival context.
Never match '琴' alone; it is a generic suffix in Chinese.
Whole-token match only.
Strings only when no other instrument; otherwise stereo.
Sax when other horn/sax tracks exist; otherwise SFX.
Minus-one deliverable (MMM). Humming backing vocals only with a vocal word ('mmm vox') or as 'hum'.
